title: Dobutamine stress imaging: reversible wall-motion defect = fixed coronary stenosis (supply-demand mismatch)
vignette: A 64-year-old man comes to the emergency department due to chest discomfort and shortness of breath. Medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and severe osteoarthritis of the left knee. The patient is an active smoker with a 20-pack-year smoking history. He undergoes dobutamine infusion with simultaneous cardiac imaging. The following is seen: before infusion, normal left ventricular contractility with ejection fraction 60%; during infusion, decreased apical contractility with ejection fraction 45%; five minutes after infusion, normal left ventricular contractility with ejection fraction 60%. Which of the following best explains the observed findings?

clues.note: Dobutamine is a beta-1 agonist that raises heart rate and contractility, mimicking exercise to increase myocardial oxygen demand - the basis of pharmacologic stress testing.

clues.text: decreased apical contractility with ejection fraction 45%
clues.note: A NEW wall-motion abnormality (drop in contractility/EF) that appears only during stress indicates a region of myocardium that cannot increase its blood supply to meet demand = inducible ischemia.

clues.text: five minutes after infusion, normal left ventricular contractility
clues.note: The defect is REVERSIBLE (contractility normalizes at rest) - this excludes infarction/scar and points to a fixed stenosis causing transient supply-demand mismatch only under stress.

whatMatters: Dobutamine raises myocardial O2 demand; a region supplied by a FIXED coronary stenosis cannot increase flow, so it becomes transiently ischemic - a REVERSIBLE wall-motion defect (contractility falls during stress, normalizes at rest). This is stable angina from supply-demand mismatch. Answer E.
strategy: Key on reversibility: the contractility defect appears DURING dobutamine and resolves AFTER. Transient = inducible ischemia from a fixed stenosis (supply-demand mismatch). Reject plaque thrombosis/MI (would give a PERSISTENT defect before/during/after), vasospasm (young patients, not dobutamine-triggered), focal fibrosis (persistent defect from old MI), and 'normal response' (normal myocardium INCREASES contractility/EF with dobutamine).

options.text: Coronary artery occlusion due to plaque thrombosis
Supply-demand mismatch due to fixed coronary stenosis

eliminations.label: Plaque thrombosis / MI - would be persistent
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: acute coronary occlusion from plaque rupture and thrombosis (acute MI). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: total occlusion causes a PERSISTENT wall-motion defect (before, during, AND after) - not one that normalizes at rest. ✅ Correct if: fixed, non-reversible defect with acute chest pain and troponin rise.

eliminations.label: Coronary vasospasm - not dobutamine-provoked
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: vasospastic (Prinzmetal) angina from transient coronary spasm. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it typically occurs in younger patients at rest and is not provoked by dobutamine (weak alpha-1 effect); this scenario is classic demand ischemia. ✅ Correct if: rest angina with transient ST elevations, provoked by ergonovine.

eliminations.label: Focal myocardial fibrosis - persistent scar
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: scarred myocardium from a prior infarct. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: fibrosed tissue is akinetic at baseline, giving a PERSISTENT defect, not one that appears only during stress. ✅ Correct if: fixed defect with a history of prior MI.

eliminations.label: Normal contractile response - EF should rise
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the expected response of healthy myocardium to dobutamine. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: normal myocardium INCREASES contractility and ejection fraction with dobutamine; a DROP in apical contractility is abnormal. ✅ Correct if: uniform augmentation of contractility and EF.

reasoning: Dobutamine increases myocardial oxygen demand (stress test)
A new apical wall-motion defect (EF 60% -> 45%) appears only DURING stress
It reverses at rest (EF back to 60%) - so it is inducible ischemia, not infarction
-> a fixed coronary stenosis limits supply during increased demand; answer E
mechanism: Stable angina results from a FIXED atherosclerotic coronary stenosis that limits blood flow to downstream myocardium. At rest, flow is adequate; during increased demand it cannot rise to match, producing a supply-demand MISMATCH and transient ischemia. DOBUTAMINE, a beta-1 agonist, increases heart rate and contractility to mimic exercise and raise myocardial oxygen demand. Myocardium supplied by the stenotic vessel cannot augment flow, so it becomes transiently ischemic and shows a REVERSIBLE wall-motion abnormality (decreased apical contractility and a fall in ejection fraction during infusion, normalizing minutes later at rest). This reversibility distinguishes demand ischemia from infarction/scar (persistent defect) and identifies a flow-limiting lesion amenable to revascularization. Normal myocardium, by contrast, augments contractility and EF with dobutamine.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid CV > stable angina: fixed coronary stenosis -> supply-demand mismatch on exertion; stress testing (exercise or dobutamine/vasodilator) provokes reversible ischemia (wall-motion defect, EF drop); reversible = ischemia, fixed = scar/MI.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Defect that appears with dobutamine and resolves at rest = inducible ischemia from a fixed stenosis.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on dobutamine, wall-motion abnormality, ejection fraction, supply-demand mismatch, or reversible vs fixed defect? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: MI/thrombosis and fibrosis give PERSISTENT defects; vasospasm isn't dobutamine-provoked; normal myocardium raises EF.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: dobutamine stress -> reversible wall-motion defect = fixed coronary stenosis (demand ischemia); persistent defect = infarct/scar.

keywords.back: Inducible ischemia from a fixed coronary stenosis
Beta-1 agonist raises HR + contractility (mimics exercise)
Fixed stenosis -> supply-demand mismatch on exertion

firstAid.detail: CV: reversible defect on dobutamine stress = fixed coronary stenosis.
CV > persistent defect = MI/scar; vasospasm = rest angina.
CV > beta-1 agonist increases myocardial O2 demand for stress testing.

memoryHook: If the weak spot only shows up when you push the heart (dobutamine) and disappears at rest, the pipe is narrowed, not dead - reversible = ischemia.
